To establish the Cactus Wellhead requirements for charpy impact testing of 
forgings, castings, wrought products such as bars and mill shapes and weld 
qualifications. Suppliers shall use this specification in conjunction with a specific 
Cactus Wellhead Material Specification (CMS) or supporting Engineering Product 
Specification Report (EPS). 
Reference 
Standards 
 
API Specification 6A, Specification of Wellhead and Tree Equipment 
 
ASTM A370, Standard Test Methods and Definitions for Mechanical Testing 
of Steel Products 
Test 
Specimens 
Impact test specimens shall be removed from a Qualification Test Coupon 
(QTC) as described in one of the following CMS’s, as applicable. 
o Cactus Material Specification CMS-001, Material Requirements for 
Ferrous Castings; or 
o Cactus Material Specification CMS-002, Material Requirements for 
Forgings, Bars and Mill Shapes 
Impact tests of a QTC shall be used to qualify a heat and the bodies, bonnets, 
stems, and end and outlet connectors produced from that heat and shall 
conform to the requirements of Table 1. 
Impact 
Strength 
Requirements 
 
Impact values for standard and non-standard materials shall conform to the 
requirements of Table 1 or Table 2. 
 
If sub-size specimens are used, the Charpy V-notch impact requirements 
shall be equal to that of the 10 mm x 10 mm specimens multiplied by the 
adjustment factor listed in Table 2. 
Test Methods 
 
Perform impact tests in accordance with the procedures specified in ASTM 
A370 using the Charpy V-notch technique as described in Cactus Material 
Specification CMS-001 or CMS-002. 
 
To quality a material for a temperature range, perform the impact tests at or 
below the lowest temperature of the classification range, in order to qualify a 
material for a temperature rating. 
 
Test a minimum of three impact specimens to qualify a heat of material. 
 
Impact properties as determined from these tests shall satisfy Table 1 or

 
In no case shall an individual impact value fall below two-thirds of that 
required as a minimum average.
Cactus Wellhead Material Specification

 
No more than one specimen shall fall below the required minimum average. 
 
If a test fails, then a retest of three additional specimens (typically removed 
from the same location within the same QTC with no additional heat 
treatment) may be made, each of which shall exhibit an impact value equal 
to or exceeding the required minimum average value. 
Specimen 
Orientation 
 
The values listed in Table 1 and Table 2 are the minimum acceptable values 
for wrought products, castings and weld qualifications tested in the 
transverse direction. 
 
Wrought products may be tested in the longitudinal direction instead of the 
transverse direction and shall meet the requirements of Table 1 and Table 
2. 


Applicable 
Cactus 
Wellhead 
Components 
and Parts 
Requiring 
Charpy 
Impacts 
Charpy Impact testing is applicable to the following Cactus Wellhead PSL 1 
and PSL 2 components and parts starting at Temperature Class P and PSL 3 
starting at Temperature Class U/V. CMS-004 will appear in the EPS bill of 
material(s) or item description when charpy impact testing is required. 
 
Valve bodies, wellhead bodies, crosses, tees; 
 
Bonnets and stems; 
 
End and outlet connectors such as: flanges, cross-over connectors, TA 
caps, tree caps; 
 
Mandrel Type Hangers; 
 
Bull-plugs, back-pressure valve bodies and valve-removal plug bodies (no

 
Actuator DAH model series: bonnet adapter, coupler, piston, rod indicator, 
cylinder, retainer dog, end cap (no PSL); 
 
Nonintegral Metal Seals such as MCS secondary seals (no PSL); and 
 
Studs, bolts and screws for Temperature Class K/L and those larger than 
2.50” thread size regardless of temperature class.
Cactus Wellhead Material Specification
